meta.name: brief
meta.description: What each session is told about this repository's plankit policy at start, generated from .pk.json

inlines.text: The repository's policy, rendered as instructions for a session. The SessionStart hook runs it on every start, resume, and compaction and injects the text as context, so a session knows the commit convention, the breaking-marker rule, the protected branches, and how plans are kept before its first command. Nothing is copied into the repository: the text is derived from
each time, so it cannot disagree with what guard, protect, and preserve then enforce.
At a terminal it prints the same text a session receives, so you can read exactly what your sessions are told;
prints the SessionStart envelope the hook emits. In an unconfigured repository the hook is silent and the command says so.
Two sentences are constant, the first and the last. Everything between follows the dials:
lists the commit types (the default table when the file leaves it empty),
decides whether the marker rule mentions the ask,
describe the protected branches and pushing,
describes how plans are kept. A dial set to off drops its paragraph.
